cards.title: Where chests go
cards.text: You said too many chests sat in dead ends. Where should they be?
cards.why: Chests are what make you explore. Too many and every dead end is a detour you have to take.

options.label: 1 in 4, plus halls
options.text: A quarter of dead ends, and one in each hall, guarded.

options.label: From camps
options.text: Clearing a camp drops its chest.

cards.title: A door to the next maze
cards.text: Your idea: keys spread through the maze open a door to a harder maze, and the wave timer resets.
cards.why: It gives an endless run chapters and a reason to cross the map, without an exit that ends the run.
cards.pick: Yes: 3 keys, each held by a camp's strongest enemy. The door shows once you hold them. Next maze is harder.
cards.details: Dying still ends the run. Your build goes with you through the door. Each maze could add a new enemy kind, so the door is also how the roster grows during a run.

cards.title: Level-ups next
cards.text: Stage 3 next: chests give modules, level-ups offer 4 upgrades for modules you have, rarity caps levels.
cards.why: That turns the build screen into the real game: you earn your build in the run instead of picking it.
cards.pick: Yes. The build screen stays as a practice room you can switch on.
cards.details: Rarity caps levels as you picked (3 / 5 / 7 / 9), with your green Uncommon fitted in at 4. Player upgrades (health, speed, cooldowns) join the level-up cards, as you asked.
